idiom_name: main()/setup building an owned Arc<Resource> (+ OnceLock for the exactly-once eager write)
implementation_notes: Rust's static and const initialisers are compile-time constant expressions, so they cannot open a socket or read configuration: runtime acquisition is necessarily explicit and owned - build the resource in main (or in the component's constructor) and hand out an Arc, which the type system keeps alive for exactly as long as it is used. OnceLock is the runtime counterpart when a static must hold the value: it is a safe abstraction over uninitialised data that becomes initialised once written, with get_or_init for a concurrent first writer and no poisoning on panic - while LazyLock is the documented lazy sibling to reach for when the acquisition must stay deferred. Pre-size collections and channels at the same point, since a Tokio runtime is itself an eagerly acquired resource built at start-up with its worker threads.
pitfalls: A static can only be written through synchronization: OnceLock::set returns Err once primed, so a second warm-up attempt (reload, second runtime) fails silently unless the error is checked.

Fallible eager acquisition belongs in main returning Result; a panic in an initialiser is acceptable only when the process genuinely cannot run without the resource, because it aborts before any graceful shutdown.

Building something that needs an async runtime - or calling block_on inside an existing one - panics with 'Cannot start a runtime from within a runtime'; build the runtime first, then the resources on it.
